pairs.why: In A the saddle sits on the top rail and its single stirrup hangs cleanly in front of the fence, but in B an extra loop appears behind the stirrup and its strap does not clearly hang from the seat over the lower rail.
A's X-legs and back posts meet the seat at the right joints and all four feet sit on the floor, while B's front cross-brace and side X-frames don't connect cleanly at the seat corners.
In A the floor runners slope at a different angle from the seat and back posts, as if seen from a second camera, while B's armchair frame, seat and feet share one viewpoint.
B's two stirrups hang side by side from a single center strap, so they couldn't hold two feet, while A's stirrup hangs from its own leather on the saddle's side.
A's labeled keys sit in rows parallel to the face edges like the real card, while B's blank key grid gives a calculator that couldn't do its job.
B shows the dome's base from above and the purple underside disc from below at once, while A's rim, lights and dome all share one top-down camera.
B's round clock stands on the floor on its rim with no stand or base, so it would roll, while A hangs flat on the wall like the real card.
A's yoke attaches to the light at only one pivot and its left arm ends in mid-air, while B's yoke grips the can at both side pivots and is clamped to the truss.
